title: Clean Hands, One Snack, One Photo
objective: Make one snack and one drink from the approved snack card using the four hygiene steps, record the work with a photo and a comment, and take the first job on the community project card.

blocks.text: BUILD · ASDAN · Week 6. ASDAN cross-strand. Clean Hands, One Snack, One Photo.

Objective: make one snack and one drink from the approved snack card, use the four hygiene steps in order, record the work with a photo and a comment, and take the first job on the community project card.
Success evidence: one snack made in step order, one photo, one comment that names a step, and one project job written down.
Every snack comes from the approved snack card. You do not talk about food at home. You do not talk about anyone's body, size or looks. You follow the card in front of you.
40 minutes. Food station and desks.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Put one snack card face up at each place before pupils sit. Check every card is from the approved pack.
stages.data-ta2: If a pupil starts on food at home, or on anyone's body or size, say we are reading the card and point at step one. Do not discuss it and do not follow it up in front of the room.

blocks.text: Hygiene is an order, not a look
Hygiene is not about how a snack looks.
A snack can look fine and still be unsafe.
Hygiene is the order you do things in.
You wash first. You clean the space next.
Then you make the food. Then you clear up.
Four steps. Always the same four steps.
Say the four step names once and leave them on the board all lesson. Pupils will need the words in their comment later.
Last week you wrote the first message to our local partner.
Today that partner gets a real job from you.
Two words matter today. Hygiene. Evidence.
Hygiene is how you work. Evidence is proof you worked.
One without the other is not enough here.
You need three things. Your snack card. Your photo sheet. A pen.
Two trays, one problem
Here are two photos of the same snack.
Both trays hold four crackers and some cheese.
One was made with washed hands on a wiped board.
One was made on a board nobody cleaned.
Look at both photos. Try to pick the safe one.
You cannot. The two trays look the same.
Germs are too small to show up in a photo.
So looking at the plate proves nothing at all.
The only proof is the order you worked in.

items: 2 · so you cannot check food by looking at it.
3 · so you check the steps instead.

blocks.text: That is why we record the steps, not only the plate.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: Stand where the whole room can see the sink. Time the hand wash out loud so pupils hear twenty seconds.

blocks.text: Four steps, in order, out loud
Watch me make the snack on my card.
My card says crackers, cheese and a cup of squash.
Step one is wash. I use soap for twenty seconds.
I dry my hands on a paper towel, not on my top.
Step two is clean the space. I wipe the board and the table.
I get my plate, my cup and my knife out now.
Everything I need is on the table before I start.

boxes.head: CLEAN SPACE
boxes.line1: wipe the board, set out the kit

blocks.caption: The four steps run one way; you never jump back
blocks.title: The four hygiene steps
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined left to right by arrows, from washing hands through cleaning the space and making the snack to clearing up

blocks.text: Step three is make. I follow the card order.
I cut the cheese on the board. I lay it on the crackers.
I pour the squash. I do not fill the cup to the top.
Step four is clear up. I do it while the snack waits.
Board washed. Knife washed. Table wiped. Bin used.
Model one card only. If a pupil asks for a second recipe, point them back to the card on their own desk.
Watch what my hands do between the steps.
I touched the bin lid. So I washed my hands again.
That is the rule. Hands to bin, hands to sink.
If you drop food, it goes in the bin. It never goes back on the plate.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits
stages.data-ta1: Deal the six job cards face down. Nobody turns one over until every table has all six.

blocks.text: Sort the cards, then match them
You have six job cards on your table.
Sort the six cards into two groups.
Group one is before you touch food.
Group two is after you touch food.
Then match each card to one of the four steps.
Hold up the card when I call its step.
Hold it up even if you are not sure.
A card I can see beats a card you kept down.
One card fits two steps. Say which one you chose.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: Take the photo only when the pupil asks. Frame hands and board, never a face.

blocks.text: A photo plus a comment
Now I record what I did.
A photo on its own is weak evidence.
My photo shows a plate. It does not show the wash.
So I write a comment under the photo.
The comment names the step and says what my hands did.
I wrote this. I washed my hands and wiped the board before I cut the cheese.
That one line turns a plate into evidence.

boxes.head: PHOTO AND COMMENT
boxes.line1: shows the step and the hands

blocks.caption: Both pages hold the same picture; only one carries a line of writing under it
blocks.title: Comment or no comment
blocks.alt: Two boxes side by side, the first with a photo and a written line under it, the second with the same photo and empty space

blocks.text: There are two more rules for the photo.
Photograph your hands and your board. Keep faces out.
No faces go in the ASDAN folder.
Take the photo while the step is happening.
A clean board at the end is not proof you cleaned it first.

items: 1 · take the photo during the step.
2 · keep faces out of the frame.
3 · name the step in your comment.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Pair pupils by table, not by choice. Call the swap at two minutes so both partners get read to.

blocks.text: Test a comment, then take a job
Work in twos. Read your comment out loud.
Your partner says which step your comment proves.
If they cannot tell, your comment has no step word in it.
Add the step word. Then read it again.
Now take the community project card off the table.
It lists four early jobs for our local partner.
Pick one job your pair can start today.
Write who the job is for. Write what you do first.
Pick a job you can finish, not the biggest one.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: Two pupils at the station at a time. Watch the sink, not the plate; step one is the one that gets skipped.
stages.data-ta2: Scribe a pupil's comment word for word. Do not tidy it into a better sentence.

blocks.text: Your turn at the station
You get one turn at the food station.
Take your snack card to the station with you.
Do the four steps in order. Do not skip step two.
Ask the adult for your photo when your hands are working.
Then write the comment under the photo on your sheet.
Write your project job line while you wait for your turn.

items: Supported · do the four steps with an adult beside you and say your comment out loud.
Standard · do the four steps on your own, take one photo, and write a comment that names a step.
Stretch · as Standard, and write the first line of your community project job.

blocks.text: Do not start until your hands are dry.
If you touch your face or your phone, wash again.
That is not a punishment. Your hands picked something up.
If you finish early, check a friend's comment for a step word.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence
stages.data-ta1: The named adult reads the comment back word for word. No paraphrase and no correction.

blocks.text: Who reads this
Two people read your work this week.
Your assessor reads the comment on the photo sheet.
Our local partner reads the job line you wrote.
Read your comment to the adult at your table.
They read it back to you word for word.
If that is not what you meant, say it again.
Your photo sheet goes in the ASDAN folder now.
Your job line goes on the project board by the door.
Next week you start the job you wrote today.

print.intro: Tick each step as you finish it. Leave a step unticked rather than ticking one you skipped.
focusRows: Four hygiene steps ticked in order, washing hands first
One photo of hands, board or food, with no faces in it
One comment that names a step and says what your hands did
tiers: Do the four steps with an adult beside you and say your comment out loud for them to write.
Do the four steps on your own, take one photo, and write a comment that names a step.
As Standard, and write the first line of your community project job.
checks: The four hygiene steps were done in order, starting with washing hands.
The snack and the drink match the approved snack card.
The photo shows hands, board or food, and carries no faces.
The comment names one of the four steps and says what the pupil did.
